title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes (a 'tame topology' project), a figure F is a finite collection of closed strata X_i. The strata are ordered by inclusion and form the poset Σ_F, and the support is |F| = ∪X_i. Page 3 defines a sub-figure F' ≤ F as a subset of strata that is downward closed (NB: if X ∈ F', Y ∈ F and Y ⊂ X, then Y ∈ F'). Sub-figures of F therefore correspond one-to-one to the down-closed ('closed', Alexandrov-topology) subsets of Σ_F. An elementary figure is one whose Σ_F has a greatest element, and F_él denotes the set of all elementary figures.

This page finishes the sentence begun on page 3: the elementary sub-figures of F correspond one-to-one to the strata of F, via X ↦ F_{≤X} = {Y ∈ F : Y ⊂ X}. So Σ'_F, the set of elementary sub-figures, satisfies Σ'_F ≅ Σ_F and Σ'_F ⊂ F_él.

F is recovered from Σ'_F, since F is the union of the strata of the F' ∈ Σ'_F. Inclusion of figures then becomes inclusion of subsets of F_él. Ordered by inclusion, F_él is a poset, and Σ'_F is a closed (down-closed) subset of it. Thus F ↦ Σ'_F is an order embedding of (figures, ≤) into (down-sets of F_él, ⊂).

In lattice-theoretic terms, figures are represented as finite down-sets generated by their 'principal' or join-irreducible pieces, the elementary figures, in the spirit of Birkhoff's representation. It is also like describing a regular cell complex by its poset of closed cells. The purpose is to reduce the global combinatorics of figures, and of their unions and intersections, to the single poset F_él. The next page then turns to the compatibility conditions (F-saturation of X ∩ X') that decide which unions of figures are again figures.
errors: No outright error. One subtlety is left implicit: an elementary figure is not determined by its top stratum X alone, since different ambient figures could put different strata inside X. The identification of the elementary sub-figure with top X in F with the one in G (when F ≤ G) depends on the NB of page 3. Granting that, F ≤ G ⇔ Σ'_F ⊂ Σ'_G holds.
The page does not say which down-closed subsets of F_él are of the form Σ'_F. Finiteness and compatibility of strata are needed; this is exactly what page 5 begins to address.

ideas.what: Elementary sub-figures of F ↔ strata of F via X ↦ F_{≤X} (principal down-sets)
ideas.modern_name: principal ideals / closures of points in the Alexandrov topology of a finite poset

ideas.what: A figure is determined by its set of elementary sub-figures, and inclusion of figures equals inclusion of these down-closed subsets of the poset F_él
ideas.modern_name: representation by join-irreducibles / down-set lattice (Birkhoff representation); face-poset description of regular cell complexes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff (1937); face posets of regular CW complexes (Björner and others)
ideas.where_published: The tame-topology programme in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) motivates it, but this formalism of figures is not published there.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine order-theoretic bookkeeping steps (down-sets, principal ideals) inside the unpublished 'figures' formalism of the 1986 analysis situs draft. The draft as a whole is of historical interest, but this page has no new result or connection.
transcription_corrections: The first line 'Strates de F.' completes page 3's sentence: '...les sous-figures élémentaires sont en corr 1-1 avec les strates de F.' The struck words after it read roughly '[-Deux ... peut être-]'.
Line 'car F est l'union des strates des F' ∈ Σ'_F' is correct as transcribed.
The '//' at the left margin before 'entre figures élémentaires' is an insertion mark, not mathematics.
